This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Package Overview

dggridR is an R package providing Discrete Global Grids (DGGs) — spatial binning using equal-area hexagonal, triangular, and diamond cells across Earth’s surface. It bridges R to the DGGRID C++ engine via Rcpp.

Common Commands

# Install package from source (run in R)
devtools::install()

# Build and check
devtools::build()
devtools::check()

# Run tests
devtools::test()

# Regenerate documentation (NAMESPACE, .Rd files)
devtools::document()

# Load for interactive development (faster than install)
devtools::load_all()
# Rebuild src/ from DGGRID submodule (run after updating submodule)
bash update_from_upstream.sh

# Regenerate coordinate conversion boilerplate (R/cwrapper.R and copy_to_src/cgen_*.h)
cd copy_to_src && python3 func_gen.py

Architecture

The package has three tiers:

R API (R/dggridR.R) — User-facing functions: dgconstruct() builds a grid spec, dgcellstogrid() / dgearthgrid() / dgrectgrid() materialize cells as sf geometries, dg_closest_res_*() selects resolution by target area/spacing.

Rcpp Bridge (copy_to_src/) — The hand-written C++ bridge that must not be overwritten by update_from_upstream.sh: - dglib.h / dglib.cpp — Transformer, GlobalGridGenerator, SeqNumGridGenerator classes that wrap the DGGRID engine - Rwrapper.cpp — RCPP_MODULE declarations exposing C++ to R - cgen_head.h, cgen_body.h, cgen_funcs.h — auto-generated by func_gen.py; do not edit by hand - func_gen.py — Generates the 30 coordinate-conversion functions (5 input types × 6 output types)

DGGRID Engine (src/) — Vendored C++ library. Entirely auto-generated by update_from_upstream.sh from submodules/DGGRID. Never edit files under src/ directly; changes will be overwritten. The submodule lives at submodules/DGGRID and tracks https://github.com/r-barnes/DGGRID.git.

Coordinate Systems

The 30 generated functions (R/cwrapper.R) convert between: - GEO — geographic (lon_deg, lat_deg) - SEQNUM — globally unique integer cell ID (most commonly used) - Q2DI / Q2DD — quad-based integer/double coordinates - PROJTRI — projected triangle - PLANE — planar (output only)

dgGEO_to_SEQNUM() and dgSEQNUM_to_GEO() are the most commonly used.

Key Design Decisions

  • src/ is regenerable — update_from_upstream.sh handles all patching (flattening include paths, renaming .hpp → _hpp.h for CRAN, removing M_2PI to avoid R header collision).
  • copy_to_src/ holds the non-generated bridge code. After any upstream update, update_from_upstream.sh copies files from copy_to_src/ into src/ as its final step.
  • The Apple Silicon numeric precision fix lives in copy_to_src/dglib.cpp and must survive submodule updates.
  • R/cwrapper.R is auto-generated by func_gen.py — do not edit it by hand.
  • Dependencies were intentionally minimized in v3.1.0: dplyr/rlang/sp replaced by collapse/s2.

Updating DGGRID

See UPDATE_DGGRID.md for the full 8-phase process. Key fragile points: 1. DgIDGGSBase::makeRF() signature — any upstream parameter change silently breaks compilation 2. New .cpp files upstream — update_from_upstream.sh only copies known directories; new files need manual additions 3. Header include regex fixes in update_from_upstream.sh are brittle and may need updating
